mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in such regimes are not statistically lower than during pre-rising periods (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer payrolls (INDPRO) indicate weakening labor market strength, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while INDPRO decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of such labor weakening events (empirical threshold).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the 12-month moving average signals accelerating demand for equities as housing construction rebounds, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average by at least 10%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months suggests supply-side contraction, which raises the cost of capital and lowers S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during INDPRO contraction are not significantly lower than during expansion (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of CPIAUCSL exceeds 3% above its trend, it indicates persistent inflation, prompting the Fed to maintain higher rates, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in such episodes are not negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in unemployment (UNRATE) and a rise in payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strengthening labor market, which typically precedes equity market strength and predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases while PAYEMS increases in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of such labor strengthening events (empirical threshold).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month accumulation of consumer spending (PAYEMS) above the 12-month average suggests building momentum in consumption, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) remains below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months, it indicates persistent supply-side weakness that raises risk premia and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO stays below 12-month MA for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during such periods are not significantly lower than during expansion (p > 0.05).
